reflections.body: Okay so intake. I basically handed them my whole file — too loud, too fast, too much feeling, shrink to keep people, then resent the little version of me who did the shrinking. I know my own tricks, is the thing. I dazzle and then I apologize for dazzling like I dropped something on the floor. Congrats Gabi, you're self-aware AND still exhausted. Two for two.

Taught the 7pm class and I was ON, everyone flying, the mirror full of arms. Then class ends and someone's laughing about something and for half a second I turn it down before I even decide to. Like a dimmer switch installed in my throat. On stage I'm the exact right amount. Real life I'm always adjusting the volume for a room that didn't even ask.

New couple came to salsa night and the woman made a face — just a flicker, probably her shoe hurt — and my whole nervous system went 'she's leaving, she hates you, wrap it up.' I read faces like weather reports and I'm always forecasting rain. Nine times out of ten it's the shoe. I know it's the shoe. I still pack the umbrella.

The self-mocking thing. I do it first, before anyone else can, like I'm racing them to the punchline about myself. If I say 'I know, I'm A Lot lol' before you do, then it doesn't count as you leaving, it counts as me joking. Clever. Also lonely. Both things.

Started the course, Fear of Being Seen. Fine. Cute title. Except I keep circling one word and it isn't 'too much' — it's 'seen.' Like I named the whole 'I'm too big' thing forever ago, that's my greatest hit, I could sell t-shirts. But there's a room behind that room. What if it's not the size at all. What if I just don't believe anyone's going to keep looking.

Over-gave at the birthday thing again. Ran the whole party, DJ'd, kept everyone dancing, three hours of pure Gabi output — and then Sunday I couldn't answer a single text. Withdrew into the couch like a possum. It's a battery I keep spending in one huge burst so nobody catches the gap between charges. If they saw the flat version, the recovery version, the tired-quiet-me... that's the one I think they'd leave.

So it was never really 'they'll leave because I'm too much.' It's 'they'll leave once I stop performing enough for it to be worth staying.' The bigness was the ticket price. I've been paying admission to my own friendships. Huh. Okay. Sitting with that one. It's uncomfortable in a useful way, like a really deep stretch.

Worksheet asked where I first learned my brightness was a problem and I wrote 'the dinner table' and then just sat there for like ten minutes not writing anything else. The table. La mesa. I could hear it before I could write it.

Ya lo escribo entonces. Baja la voz, Gabi. Baja la voz. I heard that so many times it lives in my spine, not my memory. I was seven and singing and happy and my body was just doing what bodies do and someone needed me smaller so the room could stay calm. No era maldad. They loved me. They just couldn't hold all of me at once and I decided that meant all of me was too much to hold. A seven-year-old made policy for the rest of my life. And I've been enforcing it for her ever since.

The thing that gets me is I wasn't wrong that I was a disturbance — in THAT room, at THAT table, I was. My mistake was thinking the table was the whole world. Turns out you can pick different tables. The studio is a table where my volume is the actual point. Weird how long it takes to notice the room changed.

Caught myself mid-dimmer today at coffee with Nadia and I just... didn't. Left the volume up. Told a whole story with all my hands. She didn't flinch, she laughed and did her own big thing back. Nobody died. My chest did the panic-forecast thing anyway, out of habit, like a smoke alarm going off after you already put out the candle.

Bad night. Everything piled up, class cancelled, money stuff, and I could feel a real meltdown coming, the messy ugly-cry kind, not the performative sad kind. Old me would've hidden it and texted 'haha crazy week!' three days later. I almost did that. Almost.

I let Nadia see it. Came over, I was a wreck, mocos y todo, snot and shaking and not one joke to hand her, no bit, no charm, none of the good stuff. Just the flat tired scared version. And she stayed. Made me tea. Sat on the floor with me. Didn't need me to be fun to earn the couch. I keep replaying it because some part of my brain is genuinely confused, like the math doesn't compute — I gave her the version I've been hiding for thirty years and she just... kept looking.

Starting to think 'big' and 'unsafe' were two words I glued together as a kid and have been treating as one word since. Big isn't dangerous. Big is just big. It was only ever unsafe at one specific table a long time ago. I can be enormous AND stay. Those are allowed to both be true. Nobody sent me a memo, I just get to decide.

Taught, went full volume, went to dinner after, stayed full volume, got tired, told them I was tired instead of vanishing, and went home. Whole arc, no performance tax, no possum recovery. I keep waiting to hate the small version of me and I realize — there isn't one today. There's just me, at a couple different sizes, all of them allowed at the table. La mesa es mía ahora. Loud girl included.

messages.body: hi — so I basically diagnosed myself in the intake, which is either very efficient or deeply annoying, jury's out. what do we even do when I already know all my own moves?

You know the moves — that's real, and rare. But knowing a pattern and being free of it aren't the same room. We're not here to teach you the choreography you already have. We're here to find the one step you keep dancing around without stepping through.
okay the course cracked something. I've been so proud of naming 'I'm too much' that I never noticed it's covering for something quieter underneath. give me a minute I'm still finding the words

Take the minute. When you're ready, notice the difference between 'I'm too much for them' and 'I don't trust them to stay once I stop performing.' One is about your size. The other is about whether anyone gets to keep looking.
…yeah. that second one. that's the one. that's been the one the whole time huh
the dinner table worksheet undid me a little. it all came out in spanish, which never happens in my journal, and I think that means something

It means everything. The feeling stored itself in the language it was formed in. 'Baja la voz' didn't happen in English, so of course it doesn't heal in English. Let it stay in Spanish as long as it needs to. That's not a detour, Gabi — that's the direct route.
reframe of the week: I wasn't wrong that I was too loud for that table. I was wrong that the table was the whole planet. you can just… pick a different table. mind slightly blown
And you already found one — the studio was a different table before you even had the words for it. You've been proving your own point on stage for years.
rough night. real meltdown coming, not the cute kind. old instinct is to hide and text a joke about it in three days. logging this so I have a witness to the instinct even if I cave to it
Noticing the instinct instead of just obeying it is the whole shift. You don't have to override it tonight. Just let it be visible to you. That's already new.
I DIDN'T HIDE. I let Nadia come over and see the ugly version and she stayed and made tea. I keep expecting the punchline where she leaves and it's not coming. is this what other people just have??

This is what you get to have now. Notice your brain still running the old math — 'she'll leave' — even as the evidence says otherwise. The belief updates slower than the experience. Let the tea be the proof.

big realization: I think I fused 'big' and 'unsafe' into one word as a kid. they're not the same word. big is just big. unsafe was one table, one time. writing that down felt like taking off a coat I've had on for decades
That's the separation the whole map was pointing toward. You can be enormous and safe in the same breath now. Keep the coat off — you'll be surprised how much easier you move.

went full volume all night, got tired, SAID I was tired, went home. no performance tax, no possum recovery day. la mesa es mía ahora. thank you for not letting me get away with just being clever about myself 🖤

notes.body: Intake: unusually high self-awareness — she arrives having already named nine of her own stars. 'I-am-too-much,' the performing, the self-editing, the pre-emptive mocking, the face-reading, the over-give/withdraw cycle. The work here isn't excavation, it's the last five percent she's named AROUND but not THROUGH. Two nodes she can't yet see: 'unsafe-to-be-seen' and 'if they really saw all of me they'd leave.' Careful not to over-teach — she'll out-clever the process if I let her. Confirm and connect, don't reveal.

The core surfaced in Spanish — 'baja la voz, Gabi.' Encouraged her to let it stay in the language it was encoded in; the English version keeps it at arm's length and she uses that distance to make jokes. When she writes in Spanish the humor drops away and the actual grief shows. Note the origin reframe forming on its own: the table WAS a real disturbance-management household; her error was generalizing one table to the whole world. She's finding the studio as counter-evidence unprompted. Good.

Breakthrough beat landed cleanly. She let a friend (Nadia) witness a non-performative meltdown and was not abandoned — direct disconfirmation of 'if they saw all of me they'd leave.' She's aware her belief is lagging the evidence, which is exactly the healthy phase. Watch for the 'big'/'unsafe' fusion she's now naming herself — this is the integration move. Stage 2 nearly complete; she's separating volume from danger without me having to hand it to her.
